item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.description: FABRIC is a welcoming arts and wellness series designed for adults 55+ to foster creativity, connection, and well-being. Hosted by SAIVA at Lackawanna Station in Montclair, this program brings the community together through engaging, beginner-friendly experiences. By engaging this audience, the project preserves cultural heritage, strengthens social networks, and contributes to overall well-being, aligning directly with Essex County’s commitment to arts, culture, and community enrichment. item.title: Montclair State University Campus History Tour — Wed Sep 23, 3:30 PM — Montclair State University
item.description:
Learn about the early history of Montclair State University on a 45-minute walking tour of the south end of campus. The tour will include historic photographs of the oldest campus buildings and examples of memorabilia. We will discuss student life and interactions with the surrounding Montclair community. Archivist, Paul Martinez, will lead the tour. We will meet in front of the Kasser Theater at 3:30 pm. Weather permitting – the tour will be rescheduled in the event of rain. The tour is approximately half a mile long. Most of the route is accessible. There is an approximately 260-foot section which is partially-accessible due to a steep grade. Register Here: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17668454
Hosted by: Sprague Library
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12782986
Source: Montclair State University

item.title: ARTIST TALKBACK: In Discussion with Playwright, Director & Composer of "Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy" - VIRTUAL — Wed Oct 21, 7:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Rich with emotional and social relevance, Mosaic Dance Theater Company’s world premiere production of Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy by award-winning playwright Ruth Cantrell, contrasts Greek myths to horrors of modern day, depicting the eternal existence of hate, and exploring the impact of the evils brought forth from Pandora's Box. The stories told in this piece, related by fictional characters in historical situations, are presented by a cast of 11, through live spoken word and dance, with a commissioned score of original music.
Directed by Morgiana Celeste Varricchio, with choreography by Samara Adell, and music by Michael V. Ficocelli.
This program is made possible by funds from the Essex County Division of Cultural and Historic Affairs, a partner of the New Jersey State Council on the Arts, and funding from The Puffin Foundation.
Adult Program | Virtual | Registration Required OPEN to all

item.title: Tech Talks — Thu Oct 22, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.description:
Join us for a book talk with author Nancy Burke about her book From the Abuelas' Window. The novel is currently being adapted for the musical stage!
About the book It is Chile, 1974. Pinochet has taken over the presidential palace and the government far away in Santiago. The village school in a remote farming community has been closed and converted into a detention center for political prisoners. Maribel, a young girl in the village, is protected by her mother from the truth about her father who is among the prisoners but has been moved to an unknown place.
Three nosy old neighbors, the abuelas, love to peek out their window and watch Maribel and her sisters play innocent games in their mother's beautiful garden. They are rumored to have strange, magical powers, but stubborn and restless Maribel doesn't believe the rumors. She just wants her Papa, who she believes is visiting sick relatives, back so her mother doesn't depend on the abuelas for help.

item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: NJ Death Cafe — Mon Sep 21, 7:00 PM — Freeman Gardens
item.description:
We invite you to join us for a Death Cafe. A Death Cafe is a welcoming, facilitated discussion space where people come together to talk openly and honestly about life, death, and dying—over tea, cake, refreshments, and meaningful conversation. It’s an opportunity to reflect on, explore, and share personal thoughts, emerging ideas, and lived experiences. Participants are invited to listen to and engage with others in a safe, confidential, and nonjudgmental environment while contemplating mortality. Ultimately, by talking about death, we create space to live more fully—with greater intention, presence, and purpose. All are welcome! item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Sep 29, 8:00 AM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Sep 30, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Nutrition Trends + Myths — Wed Sep 30, 2:00 PM — University Hall 2009 - Classroom
item.description:
Have you ever seen a TikTok about a new diet, food, or recipe that someone claimed "fixed all their problems?" You're not the only one! Non-nutrition professionals in media love to talk about nutrition like they're experts, but do you know how to identify the professionals from the influencers? Come to this MSDO meeting to explore current nutrition trends circulating the media, learn how to critically analyze information you view, and maybe even engage in some interesting conversations about your own nutrition beliefs. This space is welcome to all, and this includes different belief systems around food. This will not be a space to shame, guilt, or tell you if what you're eating is right or wrong. We encourage everyone to come with an open-mind and the curiosity to know more!
Hosted by: Dietetics Organization

item.title: Mindful Masculinity: A Circle of Brotherhood — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
We Meet Bi-Weekly, Every Other Wednesday · 7:00 – 8:30 PM · $15 Through open dialogue, mindfulness, and other calming practices, we quiet the mind, open the heart, and deepen our connection to ourselves and each other. The circle is open to all male identifying individuals. Meetings are hosted by Leo A. Sante – mindfulness coach, teacher, and dad. We start by sharing our wins and challenges, honoring each voice without judgment or advice. From there, we move into practices that help us release stress, shift perspective, and bring awareness and resilience into our lives. Each week centers on a different theme to help guide us – trust, accomplishment, family, rest, intimacy, presence – as we discover new ways to move through the world as mindful men. Come as you are. Leave more grounded, connected, and inspired. Connect with Leo: Instagram: @holdingpresence Online: HoldingPresence.com Email: pe***********@***il.com
Source: The Space For Art
